te: Views given on the amended principles of the draft fisheries law, continued from the previous meeting
se: The meeting continued its consideration of the draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... from the previous meeting, giving views and observations in the order of the principles amended or repealed in the memorandum of principles and reasons, and assigned the secretariat to record them for the study report
it: Draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... (Senate Rules of Procedure, rule 119)

te: Principles of the draft fisheries law considered: notices prohibiting fishing
se: The meeting noted the order appointing additional advisers and considered the principles of the draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... proposed by the Council of Ministers, in particular draft section 20 on the rules for issuing notices prohibiting the catching of aquatic animals or bringing them on board, and assigned the secretariat to use the observations in the report
it: Order appointing advisers to the subcommittee (additional)
Draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. ....: draft section 20

te: Small-scale and commercial fisheries to be distinguished by boat size, and a comparison table of the draft law prepared
se: The meeting discussed how Thailand's fisheries laws have become complex enough to burden those who make their living from fishing, for example in dividing small-scale from commercial fisheries, which should be based on boat size in line with international practice without harming marine resources. It assigned the secretariat to prepare a table comparing the draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... with the existing law, together with its principles and reasons
it: Problems and obstacles, and review of the fisheries laws
Draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... (Senate Rules of Procedure, rule 119)

te: First meeting: framework set for the study of the fisheries law
se: The meeting noted the order appointing the subcommittee and its advisers, which has 120 days to work, extendable, and set a 4-point framework: studying the facts on fisheries; studying problems and reviewing the related laws, with useful proposals; studying the draft Act amending the Fisheries Royal Ordinance B.E. 2558 (2015), B.E. .... under rule 119 of the Senate Rules of Procedure; and preparing a report for the committee
it: Order appointing the subcommittee and its advisers
Framework for the subcommittee's work

te: Floods in the North: briefing on geohazards, soil, forests and disasters
se: The meeting considered solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities, inviting the Department of Mineral Resources, the Land Development Department, the Royal Forest Department and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation to give information, such as maps of areas at risk of landslides and flash floods, community-based monitoring and warning networks, and the prevention of soil erosion. It also considered the schedule of study visits to Chiang Rai, Lamphun and Chiang Mai
it: Solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities: information on geohazards, soil, forests and disasters
Draft schedule of study visits to Chiang Rai, Lamphun and Chiang Mai Provinces (18–20 December 2024)

te: Floods in the North: 6 agencies heard, from town planning to river dredging
se: The meeting considered solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities, inviting 6 agencies to give information: the Office of the National Water Resources, the Royal Irrigation Department, the Hydro-Informatics Institute, the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning, the Department of Local Administration and the Marine Department. This covered preventive measures, water source development, town planning in risk areas, contingency plans and canal dredging. The Chair proposed that all agencies link their work and store water so that farmers can use it all year round, and 4 more agencies will be invited to give information
it: Solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities: information from 6 agencies

te: Information on floods in the North summarised, and visits to Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai prepared
se: The meeting summarised the information given by the Office of the National Water Resources and the Royal Irrigation Department on water management, flood response plans and legal and budget limits, set questions for the agencies to be invited next, and considered the schedule of study visits to Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai in December 2024
it: Solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities: summary of information and questions set
Draft schedule of study visits to Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai Provinces

te: Floods in the North: briefing by the Royal Irrigation Department and the Office of the National Water Resources
se: The meeting considered solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities, inviting the Royal Irrigation Department and the Office of the National Water Resources to give information. It felt that solving floods should start with effective preventive measures, careful forecasting of the water situation, early warnings with levels of severity so that people can prepare to evacuate, dredging of canals and rivers, and continuous follow-up of policy results
it: Solving floods in the North towards liveable and sustainable cities

te: A 3-stage work plan set, from flood relief to agro-industrial estates
se: The meeting set a 3-stage work plan: in the short term, studying solutions to recurrent floods and mudslides so that people can cope with disasters; in the medium term, studying water and soil management for agriculture; and in the long term, studying the idea of agro-industrial estates to cut costs, add value to farm products and help farmers become self-reliant. The Royal Irrigation Department and the Office of the National Water Resources will be invited to give information at the next meeting
it: The subcommittee's 3-stage work plan

te: Indicators across the whole chain, and short-, medium- and long-term plans proposed for the longan strategy
se: The meeting heard information from the agencies concerned and observed that indicators under the longan strategy should cover the whole chain from upstream to downstream, with plans divided into short, medium and long term, taking into account the benefit of growers, consumer safety, product standards, the environment and the prevention of corruption, with all sectors working together. It assigned the secretariat to use this in preparing the report
it: Draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. ....: agencies' approaches and measures

te: Questions for agencies summarised, and visits to longan orchards in the East approved
se: The meeting summarised its recommendations and questions on the draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. .... It will invite the Department of Agriculture, the Department of Agricultural Extension, the Office of Agricultural Economics and the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards to give information, and approved study visits to Sa Kaeo, Chanthaburi and Rayong on 9–11 December 2024 so that farmers' proposals can be included in the report
it: Questions for the agencies concerned
Study visit on longan (9–11 December 2024)

te: Draft longan law sections 16–18: budgets and a channel for the public to give information
se: The meeting considered sections 16–18 of the draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. .... It felt that the Longan Strategy Committee should review agencies' budget requests before they seek allocations, that agencies not following the plan must correct this within 30 days, and that there should be a channel for the public and farmers to give information when they find work that is not in line with the plan. It also set the schedule of site visits to Sa Kaeo, Chanthaburi and Rayong
it: Draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. ....: sections 16–18
Schedule of site visits to study longan growers' problems (9–11 December 2024)

te: Draft longan law sections 8–16: more farmer representatives on the board proposed
se: The meeting considered sections 8–16 of the draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. .... It observed that the longan strategy should not be reviewed every year but on a suitable timeframe, felt that the share of farmer representatives on the board should be increased and that the power to issue notices setting out working guidelines should be made clear, and agreed to visit the area to hear farmers' proposals
it: Draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. ....: sections 8–16

te: Principles of the draft longan law considered, with a focus on safety standards and the definition of growers
se: The meeting considered the principles and reasons and the sections of the draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. .... It felt that safety standards for consumers should be taken into account so that the product is accepted in world markets, that a definition of “longan grower” should be added in section 3, and that the objectives, targets, indicators and timeframes in section 6 should be made clear. It assigned the secretariat to use this in preparing the report
it: Draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. ....: principles and reasons, section 3 and section 6

te: First meeting: framework set for the study of the draft longan strategy law
se: The meeting noted the order appointing the subcommittee, which has 120 days to work, and set its framework: studying the draft Longan Strategy Act B.E. .... under rule 119 of the Senate Rules of Procedure as information for senators at the first reading; making observations and recommendations to the government or agencies on crops, especially longan; and gathering information from documents, meetings and study visits
it: Order appointing the subcommittee
Framework for the subcommittee's work

te: Holistic security: business, tax, land and religious affairs departments and the AMLO give information on foreigners; report on countering drones approved
se: The meeting invited representatives of 6 agencies: the Department of Business Development, the Revenue Department, the Department of Lands, the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning, the Department of Religious Affairs and the Anti-Money Laundering Office, to give information on foreigners coming in ways that may affect security. The holistic security subcommittee is to summarise the meetings held through November and then propose concrete approaches. The meeting approved the study report on promoting research and development of counter-unmanned aircraft systems (Counter-UAS) for presentation to the Senate; noted the work of the military affairs subcommittee, such as a study visit to the Government Lottery Office on supporting veterans' livelihoods; and approved inviting 11 military agencies to give information on readiness for the global warming crisis on 9 Dec 2026. It accepted the Royal Thai Air Force's invitation to the opening of its air operations test and evaluation on 26 Nov 2026 in Lopburi, and approved the appointment of 15 additional honorary advisers
it: Foreigners coming in ways that may affect security (the Department of Business Development, the Revenue Department, the Department of Lands, the Department of Public Works and Town & Country Planning, the Department of Religious Affairs and the Anti-Money Laundering Office invited to give information)
Study report on promoting research and development of counter-unmanned aircraft systems (Counter-UAS)

Subcommittees: the Pha Muang and Naresuan Task Forces invited to give information on border security, report on the internal security management system, study on the defence industry, and the Lopburi–Saraburi study visit
Proposal on people affected by the situation in the southern border provinces
Inviting 11 military agencies to give information on readiness for the global warming crisis and on helping the public, 9 Dec 2026
Opening of the Royal Thai Air Force's air operations test and evaluation, 26 Nov 2026, Lopburi
15 honorary advisers to the committee appointed
